issue.title: Passkey login fails with `webauthn_verification_failed` ("Backup Eligible flag inconsistency") for Apple iCloud synced passkeys on subsequent logins
issue.body:
- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 

## Describe the bug

`POST /passkeys/authentication/verify` rejects a valid assertion when the authenticator's Backup Eligible (BE) flag differs between registration and a later authentication. The client only receives the generic `webauthn_verification_failed`; the server log reveals the real cause: `"Backup Eligible flag inconsistency detected during login validation"`.

This breaks passkey login for Apple iCloud Keychain passkeys, which report inconsistent BE/backup flags before vs. after iCloud sync — producing a "first login works, later login fails" pattern. Observed in production on Apple devices (Safari/Brave, iCloud Keychain) and reproduced deterministically in a local Supabase CLI stack.

Exact server log of the failing request:

    {"component":"api","error":"Backup Eligible flag inconsistency detected during login validation",
     "error_code":"webauthn_verification_failed","level":"warning","method":"POST",
     "path":"/passkeys/authentication/verify","status":400}

The client only sees `{"code":"webauthn_verification_failed","message":"Credential verification failed"}` (the real reason is in `WithInternalError`, not exposed).

Root cause: `go-webauthn` enforces BE-flag immutability during `FinishLogin`. Per the WebAuthn/CTAP behavior of synced credentials (Apple iCloud Keychain), the BE/backup flags can legitimately differ between ceremonies, so strict rejection is inappropriate for these credentials.

## To Reproduce

Deterministic reproduction with Chrome DevTools virtual authenticator:

1. Enable a virtual authenticator (`WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator`, `ctap2`, internal, resident, UV).
2. Register a passkey normally → stored credential has `backup_eligible=false`.
3. Before the next assertion, re-add the same credential (same `credentialId`/`privateKey`/`userHandle`) via `WebAuthn.addCredential` with `backupEligibility: true` (simulating iCloud flipping the flag after sync).
4. Call `signInWithPasskey()` → `verify` returns 400 with the log line above.

Control cases confirming scope (both succeed): BE=false stable across registration + multiple logins, and BE=true stable across registration + multiple logins. Only the BE flip fails.

## Expected behavior

Relax/handle the BE-flag inconsistency for backup-eligible (synced) credentials rather than failing the login — matching the more lenient posture of other libraries (e.g. `@simplewebauthn/server` returns the backup flags for the RP to decide and does not reject). At minimum, surface the specific reason to the client instead of the generic `webauthn_verification_failed`, so RPs can diagnose without server logs.

## Screenshots

N/A (server log included above).

## System information

- OS: macOS (also observed from iOS/Safari)
- Browser: Safari, Brave, Chrome (reproduction uses Chrome DevTools virtual authenticator)
- Version of supabase-js: 2.112.3 (pinned; `auth.experimental.passkey: true`)
- GoTrue / supabase/auth: v2.195.0 (passkeys beta, `GOTRUE_PASSKEY_ENABLED=true`)

## Additional context

The strict check lives in `go-webauthn`'s `FinishLogin`; GoTrue v2.195.0 has no env/config to relax it. Reference: `passkey_authentication.go` @ v2.195.0.

## Summary

* Fixes [FE-4275](https://linear.app/supabase/issue/FE-4275/assistant-always-creates-notebooks-with-wrong-identifier-first-try): the assistant always created database notebook cells with a fabricated `database_identifier` (`"primary"`, later observed as `""` / `"_primary"` under different prompt wording) instead of omitting the key for the project's primary database, which tripped the tool's reject-and-retry validation on the very first attempt.
* Prompt wording alone wasn't reliable — live eval runs against the real model kept substituting a new placeholder every time the prompt was tightened further.
* Normalizes an empty-string `database_identifier` to absent at the schema level (`databaseIdentifierSchema` in `notebook-schema.ts`), which is inherited by every schema built from it — the AI SDK's `inputSchema` for `create_notebook`/`update_notebook`, and the write-boundary `writableNotebookSchema` used right before the PUT to the backend.
* Adds an eval case (`evals/dataset.ts`) reproducing the original bug, plus unit tests covering schema-level and write-boundary normalization.

- [X] `pnpm exec prettier --check` passes on touched files

- [X] Ran the new eval case against the real model 3x before the code fix (0% correctness, fabricated `""`/`"_primary"`) and 3x after (100% correctness)

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved notebook handling of empty database identifiers by treating them as absent.

issue.title: fix(studio): only update clicked column for composite FK inline edits
issue.body:
## I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) file.

YES

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix

## What is the current behavior?

When a user double-clicks a foreign key cell that is part of a composite FK (e.g. `role_id` in a composite FK of `role_id + tenant_id`), the Foreign Row Selector sends ALL composite FK source columns in the UPDATE payload. This silently modifies columns the user did not intend to change - for example, changing `tenant_id` alongside `role_id`, which moves records between tenants without user awareness.

This bypasses PostgreSQL's composite FK constraint checking (the database would reject a single-column update that violates the constraint, but the UI sends a multi-column update that satisfies it).

Fixes #41085

## What is the new behavior?

`onSaveForeignRow` now filters the value from the FK selector to only include the column the user actually double-clicked. If the single-column update violates the composite FK constraint, PostgreSQL correctly returns an error which is surfaced to the user via toast notification.

- Single-column FK edits: behavior unchanged
- Composite FK inline edits: only the clicked column is updated
- Row Editor panel FK selection: unchanged (user reviews all field changes before saving)

## Additional context

The fix is a 4-line filtering logic addition in `SidePanelEditor.tsx`:

```typescript
const filteredValue =
  value && editedColumn?.name ? { [editedColumn.name]: value[editedColumn.name] } : value
```

The `ForeignKeyState` already tracks which column was double-clicked (via `column.name`), so no structural changes were needed.

Added 6 unit tests covering composite FK filtering, single-column FK passthrough, null values, and the Row Editor fallback case.

Reviewed the unmodifiable-headers change carefully given the breaking-change marker.

- Map.unmodifiable is used correctly everywhere (fresh snapshot per getter call, not cached), so it can't go stale.
- Traced every internal call site across supabase, supabase_auth, supabase_functions, supabase_storage (and iceberg/vector sub-clients) via full-repo grep for '..clear()/addAll', 'headers[…]=' and similar: all former in-place mutations of client header maps now go through the new replaceHeaders()/setHeader() APIs. No missed mutation sites found.
- StorageBucketApi now copies constructor-provided headers instead of aliasing the caller's map; StorageFileApi/SupabaseVectorsClient already copied. auth_client.dart's two remaining internal 'headers' getter reads were switched to '_headers' to avoid needless unmodifiable wrapper churn, consistent with the rest of the admin/mfa/oauth/passkey sub-APIs which already used '_headers' directly.
- replaceHeaders() preserves the old clear+addAll (full replace) semantics, so no merge-vs-replace regression. setHeader() implementations preserve prior add/overwrite-single-key semantics.
- vectors becoming a per-access getter (vs a cached late final) is a real, intentional behavior change - it's called out explicitly in MIGRATION.md with guidance, and has new test coverage.
- Good test coverage: immutability (throwsUnsupportedError) for auth/functions/storage/bucket, setHeader propagation to auth admin, invoke() header precedence over setHeader, and vectors picking up updated headers.

No correctness issues or missed call sites found. Approving.

issue.title: user-feedback: warn that Edge Function secret values cannot be recovered
issue.body:
## What happened

**Task:** Configure custom secrets for a Supabase Edge Function, then use the same secret value in the Dashboard function tester.

**Skill said:** The skill correctly warned against exposing privileged keys, but it did not tell the user to save the plaintext value of a newly created custom Edge Function secret before submitting it. Later, the Dashboard showed only the secret digest, and the user could not recover the value needed for the matching request header.

**Expected:** Any workflow that creates a custom Edge Function secret and later requires the same value should explicitly say, before submission: save the plaintext value in a password manager because Supabase will only display a digest afterward and the plaintext cannot be recovered. If it was not saved, instruct the user to rotate/replace the secret rather than referring to an undefined placeholder such as `YOUR_SECRET_VALUE`.

## Source

**File:** `SKILL.md`

**Section:** `Security checklist > API key and client exposure`

## Fix suggestion

Add an Edge Function secret-handling note:

- Before saving a custom secret, store its plaintext value in a password manager when another system or request header must use the same value.
- Supabase displays only a digest after creation; the original value cannot be retrieved.
- Never ask the user to paste the secret into chat.
- If the value was not retained, rotate the secret and save the replacement before continuing.

issue.title: user-feedback: document db-tx-end requirement for rollback safety
issue.body:
## What happened

**Task:** Design a production-safe Supabase Data API smoke test for an upsert conflict target without changing real delivery data.

**Skill said:** Follow current Supabase documentation and run a test query to verify the change. The linked JavaScript rollback modifier documentation presents `.rollback()` as preventing changes from being applied, but neither the skill nor that workflow warns that the modifier only sends `Prefer: tx=rollback` and depends on PostgREST transaction-end override configuration.

**Expected:** The skill should warn that rollback preference is honored only when PostgREST `db-tx-end` is configured with an `allow-override` mode; the default commit behavior can ignore it. For production smoke tests, recommend an identical-value idempotent upsert, or require a zero-risk strict preference probe and confirmation that the rollback preference was applied before any write.

## Source

**File:** SKILL.md

**Section:** Core Principles > 1. Supabase changes frequently and 2. Verify your work

## Fix suggestion

Add a Data API verification warning: `.rollback()` is not intrinsically transactional safety. It sets the PostgREST transaction preference, which is ineffective unless `db-tx-end` permits overrides. Link the PostgREST setting, advise checking `Preference-Applied` with strict preference handling, and default production conflict-target verification to an identical-value idempotent upsert followed by a full-field reread.
